entry.title: Lifts of symmetries to minimal nondegenerate extensions are unique up to fermion attachment
entry.summary: Gauging fermion parity in a $(2+1)$-dimensional fermionic topological order requires lifting its symmetries to the resulting bosonic theory. We give a direct tensor-categorical proof that, for a slightly degenerate braided fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ and a fixed minimal nondegenerate extension ${\cal E}$, the restriction homomorphism $r\colon\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{E})\to \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LR}}(\mathcal{C})$ on classes of complex-linear locality-respecting (LR) braided autoequivalences is surjective with central kernel $\mathbb{Z}/2$, generated by fermion attachment. Thus each symmetry class has exactly two LR lift classes, related by attaching the fermion to every vortex. We apply graded Morita theory to reduce the kernel to two module types on the vortex sector, corresponding to tensoring with the vacuum or the fermion. We then prove relative rigidity to show that each type determines a unique LR class, which are distinguished by fermionic self-braiding even when their actions on simple-object labels coincide. We prove surjectivity by extending graph algebras in $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{C}$ to Lagrangian algebras in $\mathcal{E}^{\mathrm{rev}}\boxtimes\mathcal{E}$. Our results require neither unitarity nor a ribbon structure. We illustrate the lifting ambiguity in the Laughlin state, the $SO(3)_3$ theory and the Ising topological order.

entry.title: Geometry-Induced Skin Effect in Electron Hydrodynamics
entry.summary: In ultra-clean 2d materials electron viscosity is as important as Ohmic dissipation and electron transport exhibits hydrodynamic features. Using a simple framework of Brinkman equations we find that hydrodynamic electron flows give rise to a geometric skin effect: sharp obstacles locally enhance the current suppressing it far from the edges where the flow is unobstructed. This effect arises within hydrodynamic transport with finite momentum relaxation and does not rely on ballistic dynamics. Our results provide a natural hydrodynamic interpretation of edge-enhanced and double-bump current profiles observed in constricted geometries. By comparing with recent scanning NV magnetometry experiments on gated graphene, we demonstrate that such flow patterns are consistent with viscous hydrodynamics shaped by geometry, clarifying the role of geometric effects in the interpretation of electronic flow experiments.

entry.title: Bound States in Perturbative Quantum Gravity with Hydrogen-like Degeneracy
entry.summary: Recent results in the study of gravitational scattering amplitudes indicate that some highly-symmetric relativistic systems may exactly conserve a version of the Laplace-Runge-Lenz (LRL) vector in two-body bound states. We make a systematic study, in the context of a generic EFT of long-range interactions due to the exchange of massless mediator particles of spins 0, $\frac{1}{2}$, 1, $\frac{3}{2}$, 2, of the conditions for the conservation of a hidden LRL vector; both classically (no orbital precession) and quantum-mechanically (hydrogen-like degeneracy of bound states). The calculations require several new technical developments including the extension of relativistic post-Minkowskian potential matching to quantum corrections and the incorporation of long-range forces due to the exchange of pairs of massless fermions. We find that while classically the absence of precession is a generic property of a large class of models, including Kaluza-Klein theories, with vector and scalar exchanges, maintaining the degeneracy quantum-mechanically requires a surprising cancellation between gravitons and 6 Majorana gravitinos, hinting at a special role for $\mathcal{N}=6$ supergravity.

entry.title: Two Recursions for the Seiberg-Witten Prepotential: Zamolodchikov's Recursion, the AGT Correspondence and Topological Recursion on the Seiberg-Witten Curve
entry.summary: The Seiberg-Witten prepotential of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theory can be reached by two recursions of very different nature, and this thesis compares them explicitly. The first part is a self-contained review of the microscopic side: the ADHM construction as a hyperkähler quotient, the supersymmetric measure on the instanton moduli space, Seiberg-Witten theory, and the one- and two-instanton contributions computed by non-commutative resolution and localisation. The second part introduces the $Ω$-background and Nekrasov's partition function, and uses the AGT correspondence to turn Zamolodchikov's recursion for Virasoro conformal blocks into a recursion for the instanton partition function. For pure $SU(2)$, this recursion is run up to five instantons, including the first corrections in $ε_1,ε_2$. In the last part, the same quantities are obtained from the Eynard-Orantin topological recursion on the Seiberg-Witten curve, which yields the Taylor expansion of the prepotential around an arbitrary point of the Coulomb branch. For pure $SU(2)$ we give the Bergman kernel and the $B$-periods of $ω_{0,3}$, $ω_{0,4}$ and $ω_{1,1}$ in closed form. They reproduce the instanton series generated by Zamolodchikov's recursion, remain valid at strong coupling, where they detect the massless monopole, and at genus one give the first correction to the self-dual $Ω$-background. The two recursions are thus complementary: one is exact in the vacuum expectation value and perturbative in the instanton number, the other is exact in the instanton parameter and perturbative around a fixed vacuum. We formulate a conjecture relating the $B$-periods of $ω_{g,n}$ to the derivatives of the genus-$g$ free energy, and list open problems.

entry.title: Potential periodic signals in blazars: significance, forecasting, and deep learning
entry.summary: Blazars exhibit variable emission on diverse timescales. Some light curves show signs of quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs), which may encode clues regarding the physical processes behind the emission or point to supermassive binary black holes. We analyzed five blazars with previously reported high significance year-long QPOs, applying the Lomb-Scargle periodogram and Weighted Wavelet Z-transform methods to Fermi-LAT data up to early 2025. We furthermore examined an additional source (PKS 0139-09), where nascent QPO may be present. As the light curves showed longer term trends, we detrended the data using an STL decomposition, which often revealed a large seasonal component. We find that detrending generally leads to an increase in the strength of the QPO signal. However, except for PG 1553+113, where a clearly persistent QPO signal is present, we detect transience on a timescale of $\lesssim$4000 days. We then forecast the light curves over the following four years, using a traditional statistical method as well as a Transformer-based deep learning model. Applied to a test set, the latter showed significant success in predicting behavior that seems unexpected from simple inspection of the past data. Analyzing the extended time series suggests a markedly weaker QPO signals over the coming years in cases where the transient behavior appears near the end of the observational data. In contrast, in the nascent candidate QPO source (PKS 0139-09) the signal is expected to strengthen significantly. These predictions, which may reflect the physical origin of the QPOs, can be tested against future data.

entry.title: Black holes with quantum corrections in $3d$: The case of Page curve in Lindblad, greybody factor, and Lyapunov exponent
entry.summary: In this work, first we discuss black holes with quantum corrections as an open quantum system and apply Lindblad formalism to explain the ``zig-zag" behavior in the Hawking- Page curve and radiation process, specially by considering the effects of exceptional points. Then, we calculate quantum corrections for various parameters of $3d$ Cotler-Jensen theory which is $\text{AdS}_3$ with reparametrized modes. At each step of the calculations, we compare the results with the case of JT. We then calculate quantum-corrected greybody factor for various black hole solutions, and specially for the case of Cotler-Jensen theory. Finally, we study the effects of quantum corrections on Lyapunov exponent, potential, and quantum information structure of black holes.

entry.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe
entry.summary: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength. The lifetime of the sound wave source increases with decreasing $α$: for weaker transitions the source can persist for longer than a Hubble time, while for stronger transitions it decays within a Hubble time. When the walls propagate as deflagrations, the GW spectral shape changes drastically, with steeper ultraviolet tails and a shorter-lived sound wave source. We also observe that the magnitude of the normalized GWs is roughly an order of magnitude smaller than obtained in the Minkowski spacetime simulations.

entry.title: A Unified Charge-Dependent Modulation Model for AMS-02 Proton and Antiproton Fluxes during Solar Minimum
entry.summary: We develop a unified charge-dependent solar modulation model by solving the three-dimensional Parker transport equation, incorporating a realistic wavy heliospheric current sheet to treat drift effects self-consistently. Using a local interstellar spectrum from GALPROP constrained by Voyager data, we fit the model to time-resolved proton and antiproton fluxes measured by the Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer-02 (AMS-02) from May 2011 to June 2022, excluding the heliospheric magnetic field (HMF) polarity-reversal epoch (mid-2012 to early 2015). To enable rapid parameter scans, we employ neural-network-based surrogate models to compute propagation and modulation matrices efficiently. The results demonstrate that the model simultaneously describes the observed proton and antiproton fluxes with physically reasonable parameters, providing a unified account of charge-dependent modulation.

entry.title: TDCOSMO 2026: A 3% measurement of the Hubble constant from strong lensing and stellar kinematics
entry.summary: We present cosmological constraints from 11 strongly lensed quasars with measured time delays (hereafter, the TDCOSMO-2026 sample). In addition to expanding the sample, we improve many aspects of our blind analysis with respect to our 2025 analysis. Among other improvements, spatially resolved kinematics are available for nine systems, including six with JWST-NIRSpec, compared to one in 2025; for three lens models, JWST-NIRCam images now replace HST; axisymmetric dynamical modeling is applied directly to the spatially resolved data, instead of an axisymmetric correction factor applied to spherical models; and the line-of-sight convergence is now based on the Euclid Flagship simulations instead of the Millennium Simulation. Our baseline and primary result is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with a prior on $Ω_{\rm m}$ from the DES-Dovekie supernova sample. In the flat $Λ$ cold dark matter ($Λ$CDM) cosmology, we find $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$, a 3.3% uncertainty that accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. The SLACS and SL2S samples are in excellent agreement with the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, improving the precision on $H_0$ in flat $Λ$CDM to 3.0%. Using the DESI-DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) likelihood instead of DES-Dovekie yields fully consistent results. We also present constraints in the open $Λ$CDM, $w$CDM, $w_0w_a$CDM, and $w_φ$CDM cosmologies; the TDCOSMO $H_0$ inference is robust and consistent across all of them. The combination of the TDCOSMO+SLACS+SL2S likelihood with those from DESI-DR2 and DES-Dovekie disfavors $w=-1$ at the $2.3$-$2.5σ$ level in all three dark energy extensions that we tested. We find, e.g., $w_0=-0.88^{+0.04}_{-0.05}$ in $w_φ$CDM and $w_0 = -0.85^{+0.07}_{-0.06}$ in $w_0w_a$CDM, while $w_a = -0.48^{+0.46}_{-0.44}$ remains consistent with zero.

entry.title: Anyon polarons as a window into the competing phases of the Kitaev-Gamma-Gamma-prime model
entry.summary: We investigate the dispersions of anyon quasiparticles in the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid perturbed by $Γ$ and $Γ'$ couplings in order to understand phase transitions into competing states through anyon gap-closing instabilities. We demonstrate how anyon gap closings provide a way to understand phase transitions into a plethora of previously identified competing phases---including zigzag, stripy, $120^\circ$, and incommensurate spiral phases---and are in agreement with numerical studies not only on the nature of the phases, but also on the specific critical values of $Γ$ and $Γ'$ couplings. Remarkably, when the antiferromagnetic Kitaev model is perturbed by a negative $Γ$ interaction, we find that the single-vison and fermion gaps remain open while the gap of a magnon-like local boson vanishes. This points to a plausible candidate coexistence regime where long-range magnetic order emerges while fractionalized excitations inherited from the Kitaev spin liquid may persist. The magnetic order can be either stripy antiferromagnetic or incommensurate spiral, depending on the sign of $Γ'$.

entry.title: Driven Vortex Motion in Periodic Channel Potential Embedded in Superconducting Films
entry.summary: In this paper, we investigate vortex dynamics in periodically width-modulated superconducting channels by numerically solving the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) equations. The channels are designed with sinusoidally varying widths characterized by their average width and modulation amplitude. The motion of driven vortices generates an oscillatory electric field with a fundamental frequency, $f_0$, set by the channel periodicity, together with higher-order harmonics. In contrast to the situation of vortex lattice dynamics in a periodic pinning landscape of circular holes considered by Al Luhaibi et al. [1], we show that the harmonic content of the generated electric field can be effectively controlled through the channel geometry. In particular, appropriately engineered channel profiles strongly suppress higher-order harmonics, yielding an electric-field response that closely approaches a pure sinusoidal waveform. These results demonstrate that geometric modulation offers a viable route to engineering low-harmonicity microwave signals in superconducting devices and may enable cryogenic on-chip waveform generators for controlling superconducting qubits. Such devices could provide a useful building block for scalable transmon-based quantum computing architectures.

entry.title: Gauge Origami of the Conifold $\times$ $\mathbb{C}$
entry.summary: We construct gauge-origami systems on the toric Calabi--Yau fourfold $\mathcal{C}\times\mathbb{C}$ from its brane brick model. Brick matchings and phase boundaries determine elementary D6- and D4-brane framings, respectively, realizing the magnificent-four, tetrahedron-instanton, and spiked-instanton sectors in a unified framed quiver quantum mechanics. We define their partition functions by Jeffrey--Kirwan residues and describe the fixed points in terms of colored BPS crystals. General gauge-origami configurations are obtained by combining these elementary sectors through their common fractional D0-brane quiver. This construction provides a first step toward gauge origami on general toric Calabi--Yau fourfolds.

entry.title: Gravitational-Wave Propagation in Quadratic Einstein--Cartan--Dirac Gravity: A Conditional Tensor-Sector Analysis
entry.summary: We study leading tensor propagation in a specified first-order Einstein--Cartan--Dirac theory with the parity-even quadratic torsion invariant $ζT_{λμν}T^{λμν}$. Eliminating the nondynamical Lorentz connection on the regular algebraic branch gives a metric description containing the Einstein--Hilbert term, the Dirac action, and a $ζ$-dependent axial--axial fermion contact interaction. We evaluate the transverse-traceless (TT) Hessian under an explicit factorized mean-field closure, with vanishing connected-current TT response, vanishing first- and second-order TT response of the factorized current scalar, and zero intrinsic TT anisotropic stress. Under these imposed conditions, the leading two-derivative tensor action has $Q_T=M_{\rm Pl}^{2}$ and $c_T=1$, with no leading dispersion or propagation-induced polarization splitting. These conditions do not follow from isotropy of the one-point axial current, and the present calculation does not derive them from a microscopic fermionic state. The result is therefore conditional and does not establish a general Einstein--Cartan--Dirac no-go theorem. We identify the connected-current TT response that must be calculated to extend the result beyond this closure. Published NANOGrav summaries are used only to check consistency with the GR-like prediction; no new timing-data likelihood or constraint on $ζ$ is obtained.

entry.title: Creation of Viscous Dark Energy by the Hubble Flow: Comparison with SNe Ia Master Sample Binned Data
entry.summary: We study a family of cosmological models featuring dynamical dark energy (DE), based on the idea that the creation of its constituents arises from the gravitational field of the expanding universe, whose non-equilibrium physics is described by a non-zero bulk viscosity coefficient. We consider the complete scenario, in which both matter creation and bulk viscosity are present, together with its two limiting cases, in which only one of the two effects is retained. Once each model is constrained by requiring its present-day deceleration parameter $q_0$ to match specific values, the complete scenario introduces up to two additional free parameters with respect to the $Λ$CDM model, one of which is the equation of state parameter $w$ of the created dark energy. We consider two choices for $q_0$: the value predicted by the $Λ$CDM model, and one obtained from a background analysis of Fazzari et al., JHEAp 49 (2026). To perform the analysis, we construct the effective running Hubble constant, i.e. a theoretical function corresponding to the ratio between the Hubble parameter of our models and the $Λ$CDM expansion rate. The theoretical predictions for the effective running Hubble constant of the three models are tested against the Master binned sample of Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia), through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo procedure with up to four free parameters. The most important result emerging from this analysis is that, when using the cosmographic $q_0$, all three models exhibit a quintessence-to-phantom transition in the effective equation of state parameter of the dark energy; on the contrary, when using the $q_0$ coming from the $Λ$CDM limit, the transition cannot happen, and the effective equation of state parameter is entirely of phantom nature across the considered redshift range.

entry.title: Stability conditions for light rings in circular stationary axisymmetric spacetimes
entry.summary: We consider the stability of light rings in four-dimensional circular stationary axisymmetric spacetimes. Using a Hamiltonian formalism for null geodesics and the Killing symmetries of the spacetime, we show that the transverse Hessian of the geodesic potential, which controls the light ring's stability, reduces there to a pure curvature expression. Its eigenvalues are $μ_{\pm} = Φ_{0 0} \pm \lvert Ψ_{0} \rvert$, where $Φ_{0 0}$ is a Ricci scalar and $Ψ_{0}$ a Weyl scalar of a complex null tetrad adapted to the light ring. Through the Sachs optical equations, these quantities are responsible for focussing and shear of a null geodesic congruence. Stability requires both eigenvalues to be positive, so a light ring is stable if and only if $Φ_{0 0} > \lvert Ψ_{0} \rvert$ there. Assuming the Einstein field equations with generic stress--energy tensor $T_{a b}$, we recast this as $4 πT_{a b} p^{a} p^{b} > \lvert Ψ_{0} \rvert$, where $p^{a}$ is the light ring's tangent vector: for stability, the focussing by matter must dominate the local tidal shear. The trace of the Hessian alone provides an inexpensive test of stability, requiring no knowledge of the Weyl curvature, since a light ring at which the strict null energy condition is violated cannot be stable. Applying the test to specific matter models, we recover known results for vacuum and electrovacuum, with and without a cosmological constant. We also demonstrate that stable light rings are forbidden for a minimally coupled real scalar field with any self-interaction potential, since such a field must be invariant under both isometries. We show that a complex scalar field escapes this obstruction whenever it carries harmonic dependence on the Killing coordinates.

entry.title: Kink boundary-induced polarity revealed by nonreciprocal charge transport in FeTe0.7Se0.3 superconductor
entry.summary: Nonreciprocal charge transport, characterized by direction-dependent electrical response, provides a powerful probe of electronic structure and a platform for rectification. However, its realization is typically governed by intrinsic crystal symmetry, restricting the range of suitable materials. Here, we demonstrate nonreciprocal charge transport in an otherwise centrosymmetric superconductor, FeTe0.7Se0.3 (FTS), through kink boundary-induced strain engineering. The stress relaxation during growth generates a cusp-like kink-band boundary with asymmetric curvature, producing a spatially nonuniform strain field and an effective in-plane polarity that breaks inversion symmetry. Pronounced nonreciprocal transport is observed under out-of-plane magnetic fields, with strong dependence on current and temperature across the superconducting transition, in contrast to the negligible response in flat nanosheets. Our results identify kink boundary-induced symmetry breaking as a general route to engineer nonreciprocal charge transport in centrosymmetric systems.

entry.title: Re-entrant p-wave superconductivity in a Chern Dartboard Insulator
entry.summary: We formulate an exact theory for a 2-band superconductor with inter-orbital pairing and band Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) interactions. We apply this theory to a Chern dartboard insulator and compute the pair susceptibility and pair correlations analytically. We find that in the insulating phase previously predicted by BCS theory (small pairing strength $g$, chemical potential $μ$ in the gap), the HK interaction can induce superconductivity, and possibly a Chern dartboard superconductor, by lifting the doubly-occupied band and making it cross the chemical potential. From this HK-induced superconductor, we notice that in a significant parameter range (HK interaction strength $U = 1$, $μ= 0.5$), an insulator-superconductor-insulator re-entrant transition exists. We isolate the re-entrance to a conflation between HK interactions and inter-orbital pairings.

entry.title: Can a slow and strong phase transition in neutron stars relieve major compact-star observation tensions?
entry.summary: Recent anomalous compact-star observations challenge the conventional neutron-star interpretation in complementary ways: HESS J1731--347 and XTE J1814--338 favor unusually small radii at low mass, while the secondary component of GW190814 appears too massive for an ordinary neutron star under GW170817-based maximum-mass inferences. We examine whether neutron stars with a strong first-order hadron-quark phase transition can address these tensions via the extended stable hybrid branches that arise when the phase conversion is slow compared to radial oscillations, while remaining consistent with GW170817 and NICER constraints. Using a piecewise-polytropic (PP) benchmark, supplemented by an independent speed-of-sound (CS) parametrization comparison, we find two viable scenarios after a general parameter scan over both the hadronic and hybrid branches. Scenario 1 realizes an all-at-once solution: the same equation of state has a pure hadronic branch compatible with both the GW190814-scale mass and HESS J1731--347, while its slow stable hybrid branch reaches XTE J1814--338. Scenario 2 retains the GW190814-scale hadronic branch but reaches XTE J1814--338 and HESS J1731--347 on slow stable hybrid branches in very different transition-strength regimes.

entry.title: A critical coupling for the magnetic instability of holographic SU(2) plasmas
entry.summary: We show that gravity can remove the linear magnetic instability of a holographic plasma with an $SU(2)$ global symmetry. In the probe limit, charged vector bosons become tachyonic in their lowest Landau level above a critical field and condense into a vortex lattice. In Einstein-$SU(2)$ Yang-Mills theory in AdS$_5$ we include the backreaction of the field exactly, expanding only in the condensate around the D'Hoker-Kraus magnetic brane. The critical field diverges as the coupling $α= κ^2/\hat g^2$ approaches $α_\star = 2/3$, above which the normal phase has no linear charged instability at any field or temperature: we show this at zero temperature and establish it numerically at finite temperature. At zero temperature the field cancels from the mass of the lowest Landau level in the brane's AdS$_3 \times \mathbb{R}^2$ throat, and the instability is a violation of the throat's Breitenlohner-Freedman bound. The onset temperature vanishes at $α_\star$ with an essential singularity of Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless type. For two-derivative Einstein-Yang-Mills duals in $d = 4$, 5 and 6 dimensions the normal phase has a charged instability if and only if $C_J/C_T < 8/(d^2(d+1))$, one tenth in $d = 4$. Above $α_L = 0.372$ the gravitational attraction between vortices makes the uniform lattice unstable and the transition first order, so $B_c$ is only a spinodal; whether a condensed phase survives above $α_\star$ is left open.

entry.title: Thermodynamic topological classification of magnetically charged slowly rotating Kerr black holes in nonlinear electrodynamics with a cosmological constant
entry.summary: We provide an explicit rotating black-hole realization of the predicted \(\overline{W}^{1-}\) thermodynamic topological subclass by studying a slowly rotating, magnetically charged Kerr black hole in nonlinear electrodynamics (NLED). Using a reduced fixed-parameter off-shell potential, we derive the inverse-temperature curve analytically rather than relying solely on numerical plots. In AdS spacetime, this curve begins at a finite nonzero value, increases monotonically, and diverges at large horizon radius; it therefore contains exactly one defect with \(w=W=-1\) and has no stable large-black-hole branch. Positivity of the analytic coefficient establishes this result throughout the admissible slow-rotation parameter domain. Under the same reduced prescription, the Kerr-AdS benchmark instead has two branches and belongs to the \(W^{0-}\) class, establishing a clear topological distinction between the NLED-Kerr and classical rotating cases. In dS spacetime, the formally extended off-shell curve remains monotonic and any isolated zero has \(w=-1\); because the parameter-dependent horizon-admissible range is not fixed in the present reduced analysis, no physical dS asymptotic subclass is assigned.

entry.title: Limitations of Avila-inspired theory in the diamond chain with quasiperiodic disorder
entry.summary: The mobility edges (MEs) that separate localized, multifractal and ergodic states in energy are a central concept in understanding Anderson localization. In this work we study the effect of several mutually commensurate quasiperiodic frequencies on the mobility edge formation. We focus on the example of the addition of a constant offset to the quasiperiodic potential of the one-dimensional all-bands-flat diamond chain. We show that this additional offset can transform the anomalous mobility edges (AMEs), i.e. the energies, separating localized and multifractal states, into conventional mobility edges, separating localized from delocalized states. Also this appears to be the first example which shows the inability of Avila's global theory to analytically predict the ME location. We observe this both quantitatively, through the ME location mismatch, and qualitatively, via the formation of multiple MEs, not predicted by the theory.

entry.title: Chemical-Potential-Dependent Superconducting Spectroscopy on Bi2Te3/NbSe2 Heterostructures
entry.summary: High-resolution scanning tunneling spectroscopy performed at dilution refrigerator temperatures was employed to investigate the superconducting properties of topological insulator/superconductor (Bi2Te3/NbSe2) heterostructures. Coherence peaks with inner kinks or inner peaks, deviating from the conventional single s-wave spectral line shape, were observed in both 5 quintuple-layer (5QL) and 7QL Bi2Te3 thin films. Based on the combination of chemical-potential-dependent spectroscopic measurements and model simulations, we conclude that these spectral features arise from contributions of bulk and surface states in Bi2Te3 by selectively proximity-coupled to a single superconducting gap from NbSe2, rather than inheriting the complicated superconductor's order parameter of NbSe2.

entry.title: Symmetry-Restoring Counter-terms in Massive Gauge Theories with Non-Anticommuting $γ_5$ via Gauge-Invariant Sector Decomposition
entry.summary: We compute the one-loop breaking of the Slavnov-Taylor (ST) identities in a massive Abelian chiral gauge theory with spontaneous symmetry breaking, regularized in the Breitenlohner-Maison-`t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme. We also provide the one-loop finite counter-terms required to restore the one-loop ST identities. The recent formulation of spontaneously broken models based on the Fröhlich-Morchio-Strocchi (FMS) gauge-invariant and dynamical (i.e. propagating inside loops) fields is used. The proposed algebraic approach holds true to all orders in the loop expansion and allows for a consistent decomposition of the ST breaking into independent sectors. By using cohomological techniques we eventually constrain the dependence of the ST breaking on the vacuum expectation value of the Higgs field. This yields a set of differential equations that provide a useful check of the mass-dependent terms in the ST breaking terms in the broken phase. They can be generalized to the non-Abelian case, both in the gauge-invariant formalism and in the conventional one. In the massless limit we find agreement with previous calculations present in the literature.

entry.title: Origin of the high-energy spectral cutoff in gamma-ray pulsar halos
entry.summary: The spectra of gamma-ray pulsar halos exhibit a clear cutoff feature at tens of TeV. This work investigates the origin of the spectral cutoff by interpreting the HAWC data of the Geminga halo. The most straightforward interpretation is that the cutoff reflects the maximum electron acceleration capability of the central PWN. We model this scenario using spherically symmetric diffusive shock acceleration, where the upstream scale of the PWN termination shock limits the maximum energy. We also propose an alternative interpretation of the cutoff: if the electron diffusion coefficient in the surrounding interstellar medium rises rapidly at high energies, a substantial fraction of high-energy gamma-ray flux from the target source can leak outside the analysis region, producing an observed spectral cutoff effect. Both explanations successfully reproduce the spectral cutoff of the Geminga halo. Meanwhile, the two scenarios make distinct predictions on the statistical properties of pulsar halo spectral cutoffs and the X-ray spectral features of the corresponding PWNe, which may be tested through further observations.

entry.title: Static Magnetic Brane Solutions in Quartic Quasi-Topological Gravity with Power-Law Maxwell Nonlinear Electrodynamics
entry.summary: In this paper, we investigate static magnetic brane solutions in (n+1)-dimensional quartic quasi-topological gravity coupled to power-law Maxwell nonlinear electrodynamics. We derive the corresponding solutions and analyze their geometric and physical properties. We observe that the solutions are horizonless and free of curvature singularities in the physically accessible region, while the spacetime generally exhibits a conical singularity with a nonzero angular deficit at the lower radial endpoint. We demonstrate that the endpoint is independent of the higher-curvature couplings lambda, mu, and c, whereas the near-endpoint geometry is mainly controlled by the magnetic parameter q and the nonlinear parameter s. At large radial distances, we find that the higher-curvature couplings govern the asymptotic behavior of the metric. We also establish that finite asymptotic solutions require 1/2 < s <= 2 and analyze the dependence of the angular deficit on q, s, and the endpoint parameter rho_+. Using the counterterm method, we calculate the conserved mass density and show that the static magnetic brane carries no net electric charge. Finally, we verify that the power-law Maxwell theory recovers linear Maxwell electrodynamics at s=1 and Einstein gravity when lambda=mu=c=0.

entry.title: ELISA: A Bayesian X/$γ$-ray Spectral Analysis Toolkit
entry.summary: Forward-folded X/$γ$-ray spectral fitting increasingly benefits from Bayesian workflows to better capture counting statistics, background uncertainties, and complex parameter degeneracies, while fully reproducible end-to-end implementations are still not always straightforward to deploy in routine analyses. We present ELISA (Efficient Library for Spectral Analysis), an open-source Python toolkit that streamlines the full spectral analysis loop for X/$γ$-ray astronomy: data loading, model construction, inference, and model validation and comparison. ELISA couples a JAX-accelerated forward model with a unified fitting interface, supporting both rapid optimization and modern Bayesian sampling. Built-in diagnostics make convergence checks and predictive assessment a standard part of the workflow, motivating principled model refinement when needed. Using a spectral fitting example of the Insight-HXMT Crab observation, we find substantial improvements in sampling efficiency compared with XSPEC's default MCMC implementation. ELISA is available at https://github.com/wcxve/elisa and on PyPI at https://pypi.org/project/astro-elisa.

entry.title: Magnetar X-ray flares as elementary reconnection events in a self-organized critical magnetosphere
entry.summary: Magnetar bursts are commonly attributed to magnetic energy release, yet the physically relevant dissipation unit has remained uncertain. Here we argue that this unit is not the burst as conventionally defined, but the short substructures within bursts, namely magnetar X-ray flares (MXFs). Using 789 MXFs from SGR~J1935+2154, we show that their waiting times separate into two components, interpreted as reflecting clustered intra-episode events and longer inter-episode intervals, that their proxy emission measure and temperature exhibit distinct rising and declining trends, and that their energy release scale (ERS) proxy distribution has a high-end slope in the same statistical regime as solar and stellar flares. Combined with the previously measured MXF duration slope, these results identify MXFs as a three-dimensional fractal-diffusive self-organized critical (FD-SOC) system with $β_{\rm diff}\simeq2$, implying reconnection avalanches that expand linearly through an active magnetosphere. We infer that magnetar active episodes are global unloading states assembled from many elementary flares. Magnetar X-ray flares are therefore the physically relevant units for magnetar outburst statistics and for connecting magnetar high-energy activity to other impulsive phenomena.

entry.title: Exotic metallic phase in a heterotic Kondo lattice: violation of Luttinger's theorem and absence of Kondo gap
entry.summary: Fermi surface transformation accompanied by quantum phase transition is widely observed in correlated electron systems including heavy fermion materials and van der Waals quantum heterostructures. The unified Anderson lattice description for this phenomenon suggests that their interacting ground states in the case of electron half filling always destabilize the metallic phase in the strong Kondo-coupling regime. We examine this issue within the paramagnetic phase of a Kondo lattice system with a heterotic layered structure. In the weak Kondo-coupling regime, the system exhibits a fractional Dirac liquid involving the massless or massive Dirac fermions and a charge neutral spinon Fermi surface. In the strong Kondo-coupling regime, the spinons hybridize with the Dirac fermions resulting in an intermediate nearly-flat hybridizing band together with the conduction and valence heavy fermion bands, yielding a large electric Fermi surface. Absence of the Kondo gap between these bands is observed depending on the stacking configurations of the layered structure. In particular, the system remains metallic even at the exact half filling in this regime and Luttinger's theorem is violated across the critical point. Implications of these results on the van der Waals quantum heterostructures are briefly discussed.

entry.title: Near-Horizon Deformation of Metric and the Black Hole Instability
entry.summary: Recent time-domain analyses suggest that black hole stability may be sensitive to localized near-horizon geometric deformations, while the underlying spectral mechanism remain unclear. In this work, after verifying the instability of the model in the time domain, we systematically investigate quasi-normal mode spectra under static localized non-positive perturbations within a frequency-domain framework. We find that such deformations generically induce a new purely imaginary mode. As the deformation approaches the horizon, the imaginary part of this mode increases and eventually enters the upper half complex-frequency plane, signaling the onset of black hole instability. Numerical results reveal clear scaling relations between the critical distance for instability and the deformation strength. We further derive rigorous proofs for our discoveries in frequency domain. These results demonstrate that black hole stability under long scale is conditionally sensitive to localized deformation of metric near the horizon and establish a unified spectral framework for understanding their induced instabilities.

entry.title: Impact of Decay-Chain Feeding by Long-Lived Heavy Nuclei on Nuclear Cosmochronology
entry.summary: Nuclear cosmochronology provides an independent method for determining the ages of astrophysical objects without relying on Galactic chemical evolution models. Long-lived radioactive actinides synthesized via the rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) particularly thorium and uranium serve as ideal chronometric nuclei. However, predicting the initial abundances of these nuclei and their subsequent long-term evolution remains a major source of uncertainty in nuclear cosmochronology. In this work, we investigate the impact of decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei on nuclear cosmochronology and estimate the corresponding age corrections. We develop a self-consistent radioactive decay network that includes all relevant decay pathways and couple it to $r$-process nucleosynthesis calculations. By tracking the long-term evolution of $r$-process nucleosynthesis based on neutron star merger trajectories, the dominant long-lived nuclei shaping the evolution of the chronometric elements Th and U are identified as $^{232}$Th, $^{235}$U, $^{236}$U, $^{238}$U, and $^{244}$Pu. It is found that delayed feeding substantially modifies the long-term evolution of actinides particularly for $^{232}$Th, which receives significant late-time contributions from heavier progenitor nuclei such as $^{244}$Pu and $^{236}$U. As a consequence, the U/Th and Th/X chronometers exhibit significant sensitivity to delayed feeding from the progenitor nuclei $^{244}$Pu and $^{236}$U, with age corrections reaching $\sim5$~Gyr. These results suggest that decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei plays a crucial role in nuclear cosmochronology and should be properly accounted for in age determinations based on actinide chronometers.

entry.title: Reawakening of GS 1843+00: A Multiwavelength Study of its 2026 Giant X-ray Outburst
entry.summary: GS 1843+00 (Ginga 1843+009) is a poorly studied Be/X-ray binary system that underwent a major X-ray outburst in 2026 February-May after nearly sixteen years of quiescence. We present an X-ray, optical, and radio study of GS 1843+00 during this outburst, focusing on the evolution of the neutron star emission geometry, Be-disk connection, and possible outflow activity. We analyse three NuSTAR observations obtained at different stages of the outburst, complemented by archival RXTE and Chandra data, optical spectroscopy and imaging with the Nordic Optical Telescope, and a MeerKAT radio observation. NuSTAR observations reveal coherent X-ray pulsations around 29.7 s with a spin-up rate of $(-5.1\pm0.1)\times10^{-8}$ s s$^{-1}$ during the outburst. The pulse profiles show strong evolution with energy and outburst phase, with distinct morphologies even at comparable luminosities. The pulsed fraction varies between 1 and 16% and exhibits a complex reversal in energy dependence above 7 keV, increasing with energy during the first two observations and decreasing during the third. The 3-79 keV broadband spectra are described by thermal Comptonization with a blackbody and an Fe K$α$ emission line, with no evidence for a cyclotron absorption feature. Phase-resolved spectroscopy reveals variations in the Comptonization and blackbody parameters, indicating changes in the accretion-column structure. Optical spectroscopy confirms the presence of a Be-circumstellar disk through H$α$ and Paschen-series emission lines. No radio counterpart is detected, with a $3σ$ upper limit of 36 $μ$Jy beam$^{-1}$ at 1.28 GHz. Weaker H$α$ emission compared with previous epochs indicates that the Be-circumstellar disk was in a different state during the current episode, while the radio non-detection suggests that any associated outflow activity was faint or below the detection limit.

entry.title: Bondi Four-Momentum Balance in Quantum NSF Classical matching, DKL supermomentum, and quantum energy redistribution
entry.summary: We derive Bondi four-momentum balance between past and future null infinity in the radiative phase space of the null-surface formulation (NSF). Weyl matching at spatial infinity, together with vanishing endpoint News, gives antipodal continuity of the Bondi mass aspect. Its translation projection is independent of the infrared shear term and transforms as a Lorentz four-vector. Bondi evolution relates the incoming and outgoing News fluxes to the timelike endpoint momenta; in the Dominguez--Kozameh--Ludvigsen radiative sector these momenta vanish and the fluxes are equal. On a common radiative Fock domain, unitary conjugation transports the flux observables. Adopting their classical balance as an additional quantum condition yields exclusive four-momentum conservation. We also calculate the outgoing energy expectation without imposing that condition. For an incoming energy eigenstate, the second-generator commutator vanishes diagonally, leaving a second-order coefficient determined by the cubic generator. Direct canonical contractions isolate the contribution connected to all four external legs. For the equal-energy center-of-mass preparation, axial rotational covariance forces the angularly integrated exchange coefficient to vanish under the finite helicity-projection prescription of Part~I. The connected energy defect therefore vanishes through second order. The full expectation (including spectators) and higher-order balance remain open.

entry.title: Quantum Geometry and Pair Breaking in Intra- and Intervalley Superconductivity of Rhombohedral Graphene
entry.summary: The observation of superconductivity emerging from a spin- and valley-polarized normal state in rhombohedral graphene raises a basic puzzle: intravalley Cooper pairs involve states that are not generically degenerate because of trigonal warping, and therefore lack the particle--particle nesting underlying the conventional Cooper instability. While recent model studies suggest that nontrivial band geometry can strongly promote chiral pairing, how this geometric enhancement competes with realistic band-structure-induced pair breaking remains unclear. Here we study Kohn--Luttinger superconductivity in electron-doped rhombohedral tetralayer graphene using a DFT-fitted multiorbital tight-binding model, retaining the full Bloch-wave-function form factors in both RPA screening and the projected Cooper interaction. We separate the superconducting instability into three contributions: the symmetry-resolved form-factor-dressed interaction, the Cooper-pair phase space determined by the symmetrized pair dispersion, and the energy mismatch generated by trigonal warping. We find that the Bloch form factors strongly favor intravalley pairing, with a leading predominantly $p_x-ip_y$ instability and a substantially larger maximum $T_c$ than the intervalley reference state. At the same time, trigonal-warping-induced mismatch cuts off the Cooper logarithm and confines intravalley superconductivity to a much narrower region of the phase diagram. The dominant instability occurs near pair-Lifshitz transitions and primarily in reconstructed annular or three-lobed Fermi-surface regimes. Our results show that superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene is controlled by the combined effects of quantum-geometry-dressed interactions, pair fermiology, and trigonal-warping-induced pair breaking.

entry.title: On Ising model in magnetic field on the lattice
entry.summary: We study the free energy of the classical square-lattice Ising model in a uniform real magnetic field $h$, for which no exact solution is known. We first conjecture a closed-form expression built from the one-dimensional Ising chain and Onsager's hypergeometric solution. Comparing with high-precision tensor renormalization group (TRG) data, we find that it deviates by up to $2.6\%$, has no spontaneous magnetization, and gives an effective critical-isotherm exponent $δ\to 1$. However, using the Lee--Yang circle theorem, we show that the exact free energy is a superposition of one-dimensional Ising chains in the same field, weighted by a temperature-dependent (normalized, but not always positive) distribution of squared Lee--Yang gaps, of which our first expression is a single-chain approximation. Exact results (Onsager, Yang, the strong-field expansion and the Lee--Yang solution at $βh = iπ/2$) become sum rules for this distribution. We propose a simple form for it, fixed by Onsager's free energy and the exact strong-field limit without any fit to numerical data. This \emph{improved} conjecture agrees with TRG to $0.15\%$ for all $β$ and $h$, reproduces Yang's spontaneous magnetization exactly, has a positive specific heat, and yields the critical isotherm $M\propto h^{1/δ}$ with $δ= 15.2$ and amplitude $1.055$, compared with the exact $δ=15$ and $1.059$. A refined form, which builds in additional input from Ising field theory (including the exact critical isotherm, $δ=15$) and a few constants adjusted to transfer-matrix and TRG data, matches the TRG free energy to $4\times 10^{-5}$.

entry.title: A note on decoherence in quantum cosmology by thermal perturbations: an open quantum systems approach
entry.summary: We study, within a toy model, how a thermal bath of cosmological perturbations can decohere the minisuperspace degrees of freedom of the universe, treating the perturbations as an environment in the framework of open quantum systems. Instead of tracing out the perturbations from a semiclassical ansatz for the total wave function, as in earlier approaches, we incorporate their backreaction on the background through an effective second-order coupling and derive a master equation. The model describes a spatially flat semiclassical universe during slow-roll inflation with a dust clock field, while scalar cosmological perturbations in a phenomenologically assumed thermal state constitute the environment. The master equation is non-Markovian, since the bath correlation functions do not decay in time. Within this framework, we find that, for a representative set of parameter estimates, the characteristic decoherence timescale corresponding to the thermal contribution can be shorter than the Hubble timescale. In addition, we address the question of whether the pointer-state structure induced by the decoherence in such a framework could provide a criterion for the choice of semiclassical states in quantum cosmology.

entry.title: PINNs for N=2* holography
entry.summary: Can a holographic theory be reconstructed from its equation of state? We investigate this question using physics-informed neural networks in the bosonic-mass sector of the Pilch--Warner model. We first validate the PINN approach against an analytic solution encoding the leading high-temperature corrections to the conformal equation of state. We then reconstruct nonlinear black-brane geometries and the scalar potential using thermodynamics, ultraviolet asymptotics, Ward identities, and horizon regularity. Independent solutions of the bulk Einstein-scalar equations demonstrate that accurately reproducing thermodynamics with a trained PINN does not guarantee an accurate reconstruction of the scalar potential. High-precision knowledge of the high-temperature equation of state constrains nonlinear interactions in the bulk scalar potential. Fixing the cubic coupling to its exact PW value, motivated by this high-temperature extraction, reduces the maximum sampled error in the reconstructed scalar self-interactions by a factor of $\sim 15$ compared with constraining only the bulk scalar mass. Adding knowledge of the bulk viscosity of the gauge theory plasma further reduces this error by an additional factor of $\sim 13$, with independent forward solutions reproducing the bulk viscosity within $0.09\%$.

entry.title: CMB Data Analysis in the example of the POLARBEAR experiment and the LiteBIRD experiment
entry.summary: In this dissertation, I briefly go through my subject areas --- from Astrophysics, Cosmology, to Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) radiation; and Data Science & High-Performance Computing. I go through the beginning of the Universe briefly in part I and introduce the Physics of the CMB in part II. Then I move on to how it can be observed experimentally, mathematically, and computationally in part III. In parts IV to VI, I write about 2 specific CMB experiments --- POLARBEAR & LiteBIRD, together with my research involved in them. In part V, original research on a measurement of the CMB $B$-mode at sub-degree scales is presented using the 3rd-5th seasons of POLARBEAR observations. This demonstrates the capability of a single medium aperture telescope with a Continuously Rotating Half-Wave Plate (CRHWP) to target both the low-$\ell$ and high-$\ell$ $B$-mode science at $50 \leq \ell \leq 3000$. In part VI, the effect of detector crosstalk systematics on the CMB power-spectra is studied in detail in the example of the LiteBIRD experiment. An analytical, map-domain solution is developed, a computational simulation method is implemented, and the two predictions are compared using the LiteBIRD experiment design specification. The general agreement of the two shows that the analytical model well describes the LiteBIRD experiment, and can be used to calculate the systematic effects without performing time-consuming time-domain simulations with a high degree of accuracy. This can be used to forecast the amount of crosstalk systematics and to develop mitigation strategies. A mitigation strategy is presented, which is a hardware-based mitigation method that minimizes the crosstalk systematic effects in the 2pt power-spectra.

entry.title: Characteristic Modes of Non-minimally Coupled Thick Branes
entry.summary: Characteristic modes provide important information about the intrinsic properties and dynamical response of gravitational systems. In this work, we investigate characteristic modes of thick branes with a non-minimally coupled bulk scalar field. Two representative thick brane solutions are considered, corresponding to a single-kink scalar configuration and a deformed kink configuration with internal structure, respectively. By analyzing the tensor perturbation equations, we first examine the localization of the graviton zero mode in the two brane models. For both brane models, the graviton zero mode is localized on the brane. No pronounced resonant Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes are found for the single-kink brane at $ξ=1/7$. For the deformed brane, we investigate the resonant KK modes at $ξ=0.99$, finding that increasing the deformation parameter $k$ leads to more resonant modes and a longer-lived first resonance. We then calculate the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of both brane models independently in the frequency and time domains. The quasinormal frequencies (QNFs) obtained by the independent methods agree well for the low overtones. The masses and decay rates of the resonant KK modes agree closely with the real parts and the magnitudes of the imaginary parts of the corresponding QNFs, respectively.

entry.title: Pre-pairing and polarization of doped charge carriers in unconventional superconductors
entry.summary: Based on first principles calculations, we show in hole-doped La2-xSrxCuO4, the Sr dopants prefer to form dimers, rather than be isolated as generally believed. Same trend applies to other superconductors such as Na-doped Ca2CuO2Cl2, and electron type Nd2-xCexCuO4. The dimer structure makes the two doped holes (electrons) bound up and form a singlet which is also polarized. Another type of dopant in cuprates is oxygen which behaves similarly. So, we propose that, for all oxide high TC superconductors, the holes (electrons) are pre-paired (Z-pairs) during the preparation of the superconductor. The spontaneously formed Z-pairs are conceptually different from not only the Cooper pairs, but also the Zhang-Rice singlets. The attraction force in a Z-pair originates basically from the strong antiferromagnetic exchange energy. We also found that the on-site Coulomb repulsion (U) is no longer a constant due to doping. Around a doping site, U can reduce its value discontinuously, which plays a key role in stabilizing the Z-pairs against isolated holes (electrons). A Z-pair is a p-wave like localized state which breaks the symmetry of the CuO2 plain and attracts each other along the direction perpendicular to the polarization. The Z-pairs may be popular in all of the unconventional superconductors and the periodic assembly can result in the emergence of coherence states and superconductivity.

entry.title: Spotting Stasis in Cosmological Perturbations
entry.summary: As discussed in a number of recent papers, cosmological stasis is a phenomenon wherein the abundances of multiple cosmological energy components with different equations of state remain constant for an extended period despite the expansion of the universe. One of the most intriguing aspects of the stasis phenomenon is that it can give rise to cosmological epochs in which the effective equation-of-state parameter $\langle w \rangle$ for the universe is constant, but differs from the canonical values associated with matter, radiation, vacuum energy, etc. Indeed, during such a stasis epoch, the spatial average of the energy density of the universe evolves in precisely the same manner as it would have evolved if the universe were instead dominated by a perfect fluid with an equation-of-state parameter equal to $\langle w \rangle$. However, as we shall demonstrate, this equivalence is broken at the level of the perturbations of the energy density. To illustrate this point, we consider a stasis epoch involving matter and radiation and demonstrate that within this stasis background the density perturbations associated with a spectator matter component with exceedingly small energy density exhibit a power-law growth that persists across the entire duration of the stasis epoch. This growth can potentially lead to significant enhancements of structure at small scales. Such enhancements are not only interesting in their own right, but may also provide a way of observationally distinguishing between a stasis epoch and an epoch of perfect-fluid domination -- even if the universe has the same equation of state in both cases.

entry.title: Non-Stationary Wormholes and Matter Source Reconstruction in General Relativity
entry.summary: We investigate non-stationary wormhole geometries in General Relativity embedded in evolving cosmological backgrounds. We employ a Simpson-Visser-like regularization of the temporal coordinate of the $(n+1)$-dimensional FLRW metric, together with a homogeneous Cuscuton field, to construct cosmological backgrounds in which the scale factor remains finite and non-zero at the would-be initial singularity. We then consider two specific dynamical wormhole geometries: the four-dimensional defect wormhole and the topologically charged Perry-Mann type wormhole. We show that the former can be supported by a canonical scalar field with vanishing potential, while the latter requires a mimetic matter sector to support its spatial structure, with the Cuscuton governing the cosmological evolution in both cases. We subsequently generalize the analysis to a separable non-stationary spacetime and derive a scaling condition that strongly constrains the admissible matter sources. In particular, for minimally coupled scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics fields, this condition removes the functional freedom available in static reconstruction schemes. We show that, within this framework, regular, asymptotically flat wormhole geometries cannot be obtained while simultaneously satisfying the required smoothness and reflection symmetry conditions. Our results illustrate both the possibility of constructing specific non-stationary wormholes in regular cosmological backgrounds and the restrictions that arise when attempting to generalize such constructions to arbitrary spatial geometries.

entry.title: No-Go Theorem for Phantom Crossing in Scalar-Tensor Gravity with Non-Minimal Derivative Coupling and Soft Scale-Invariance Breaking
entry.summary: Recent baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI 2024) reveal a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state parameter crossing the phantom divide ($w < -1$) at low redshifts. We investigate whether this phantom crossing can be realized within scale-invariant scalar-tensor theories featuring non-minimal derivative coupling (NMDC) between the scalar field and the Einstein tensor. Employing the effective field theory of dark energy formalism, we systematically derive the ghost-free and gradient stability conditions, and examine their compatibility with the swampland conjectures from quantum gravity. We establish three rigorous no-go theorems demonstrating that: (i)~phantom crossing necessitates $ξ_{\text{eff}} < 0$, directly violating the no-ghost stability requirement $ξ_{\text{eff}} > 0$; (ii)~the swampland de Sitter and distance conjectures independently obstruct phantom crossing; and (iii)~these theoretical obstructions are mutually reinforcing. Our results show that scale-invariant NMDC models cannot account for the DESI preference for $w < -1$, providing robust theoretical guidance for dark energy model building beyond this class.

entry.title: The effect of triples on the Chemically Homogeneous Evolution Channel for producing Gravitational Wave Sources
entry.summary: Despite the growing number of gravitational-wave (GW) detections, the formation of merging binary black holes (BBHs) is still debated. One of the proposed formation channels is Chemically Homogeneous Evolution (CHE), which makes distinct predictions for the properties of the resulting black holes (BHs): high masses ($\gtrsim35\, M_\odot$) and large, orbitally-aligned spins. These predictions are based on studies that consider this channel only in isolated binaries. However, most massive stars reside in triples. We investigate how a tertiary affects the CHE channel. We use detailed binary models computed with MESA for the inner CHE systems coupled with analytical prescriptions for the hierarchical triple dynamics. Specifically, we study the von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai mechanism that can accelerate the merger of the inner BBHs through high-eccentricity excitations. We show that a tertiary companion enables mergers at higher metallicities, where the classical binary CHE channel does not operate. At $Z_\odot/3$, triples produce BHs with lower masses (around $15\,M_\odot$) and lower spins (around 0.25) compared to the low-metallicity classical scenario. We further expect triple dynamics to lead to spin-orbit misalignment and potential residual eccentricities at merger. In triples at $Z_\odot/3$, half of the mergers occur within 1 Gyr. Moreover, 10% of the population leads to prompt mergers within 1 Myr (1% within 1 kyr) that are of potential interest for electromagnetic counterparts. We conclude that the triple CHE channel is promising as (i) it may contribute more substantially to the local merger rate than had been expected for the classical CHE channel due to the shorter delay times and effectiveness at higher metallicities and (ii) produces mergers with properties that more closely resemble the lower masses and lower spins inferred for most of the observed GW merger population.

entry.title: One-loop QED effective action at finite temperature and density beyond HTL limit
entry.summary: We develop a framework for computing the nonlocal one-loop effective action in scalar and spinor QED at finite temperature and chemical potential in arbitrary even spacetime dimensions. Based on the heat kernel expansion to quadratic order in background fields, the framework reduces the effective action form factors to a common fundamental kernel. By resumming the external-momentum expansion, we obtain explicit closed-form expressions for the massless form factors in terms of polylogarithms and their derivatives with respect to the order. The same method determines the coefficients of the small-mass expansion to arbitrary order. The resulting expressions retain the full dependence on external Euclidean momentum, temperature, and chemical potential, without invoking the soft-momentum approximation. We also derive the corresponding photon polarization operators and evaluate their static limits, obtaining the Debye screening masses and electromagnetic susceptibilities.

entry.title: Numerical methods and analytic results for one-dimensional strongly interacting spinor gases
entry.summary: One of quantum physics' fundamental, but largely unsolved, problems is the computation of the correlation functions in many-body systems. In this paper we address this problem in the case of one-dimensional spinor gases with repulsive contact interactions in the presence of a confining potential. We take advantage of the fact that in the strong coupling limit, the wavefunction factorizes with the charge degrees of freedom expressed as a Slater determinant of spinless fermions and the spin sector described by a spin chain of Sutherland type with exchange coefficients that depend only on the trapping potential. This factorization is also present in the expressions for the correlation functions. Still, analytical and numerical investigations were hindered by the fact that the local exchange coefficients and the charge component of the correlators are expressed as $N-1$ multidimensional integrals, with $N$ the number of particles, which are notoriously hard to compute using conventional methods. We introduce a new approach to calculating these integrals that is extremely simple, scales polynomially with the number of particles, and is several orders of magnitude faster than the previous methods reported in the literature. This allows us to investigate the static and dynamic properties, temperature dependence, and nonequilibrium dynamics for systems with a larger number of particles than previously considered and discover new phenomena. We show that, contrary to natural expectations, the momentum distribution of strongly interacting trapped spinor gases becomes narrower as we increase the temperature and derive simple determinant representations for the correlators in the spin incoherent regime valid for both equilibrium and nonequilibrium situations.

entry.title: Observational Indistinguishability and the Beginning of the Universe
entry.summary: Can we infer whether all of physical reality began to exist? Several novel results are offered suggesting a negative verdict. First, two necessary (but not necessarily sufficient) conditions are offered for a cosmic beginning. Second, I discuss three theorems which show that, in a wide range of spacetimes, observers cannot infer the global structure of their spacetime; one of the three shows that spacetimes satisfying a condition necessary for a cosmic beginning are observationally indistinguishable from spacetimes which do not satisfy that condition. Next, I offer two extensions to the aforementioned theorems. The two extensions show that, in an equally wide range of spacetimes, observers cannot collect sufficient data to determine whether the application conditions for the class singularity theorems are satisfied or whether their spacetime satisfies the two necessary conditions for a cosmic beginning. Lastly, a reply is offered to the objection that the skeptical consequences of the aforementioned theorems can be overcome with induction. Importantly, all past singular dust FLRW spacetimes are observationally indistinguishable from counterparts which, while sharing a number of important local properties, either do not include a singularity to the past of every point or else do not have the sort of time ordering intuitively required for a cosmic beginning.

entry.title: Gravitational redshift of broadband relativistic quantum photons
entry.summary: Gravitational redshift is a key prediction of general relativity that has been experimentally verified. Nevertheless, its existence in the context of relativistic and quantum physics has not yet been established. We employ linearized quantum gravity to study the effects of quantum coherence on gravitational redshift of broadband photons that interact with a planet via graviton exchange. We find that gravitational redshift, as predicted by general relativity, occurs when the initial photonic state contains no quantum coherence between orthogonal photonic modes, such as position states. If quantum coherence is initially present, different photonic modes overlap, a genuine quantum correction occurs solely for single-photon states. Our work not only explains gravitational redshift as the interaction of gravitons and photons in flat spacetime, but also shows that deviations from the theory occur already at low energies when quantum interference of photonic states is important.

entry.title: Three-dimensional vacua of $G_2$ flux compactifications
entry.summary: We study supersymmetric vacua of three-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ effective theories from type IIA, type IIB/type I, and heterotic compactifications on $G_2$-structure spaces. Superpotential homogeneity and the physical scalar metric yield universal vacuum relations and axion stabilization constraints without specifying the full moduli-space metric. We express AdS$_3$ scalar masses through $Δ$, the scaling dimension of the corresponding operator in the dual two-dimensional conformal field theory. In massive type IIA AdS$_3$ vacua, we derive the bound $Δ_{\max}\geq(20+4\sqrt{67})/7\approx 7.5$ and an exact dimension $Δ_b=6$ for $B_2$ axions on the torsion-free branch. Type IIB type I and heterotic AdS$_3$ vacua contain a universal volume-dilaton mode with $Δ_{φs}=4$. On the singlet-torsion type IIB branch, we also obtain the volume-dilaton mode with $Δ_{φs}=20/7$ and $Δ_b=16/7$. Every supersymmetric Minkowski vacuum in the retained classical closed-string theories possesses an exact volume-dilaton flat direction. We characterize physical large-flux limits after tadpole constraints and axionic identifications, and identify torsion obstructions to isotropic scale separation.

entry.title: The dimensional reduction of the spin-3 and spin-4 partially broken Fronsdal models
entry.summary: Here we perform a Kaluza-Klein dimensional reduction from $D+1$ to $D$ dimensions of a partially broken Fronsdal model for spin-3 and spin-4. The reduced models describe massive spin-3 and spin-4 particles without extra propagating modes. They differ from Singh-Hagen models by quadratic terms which vanish on shell, similarly to their higher dimensional massless parents. A covariant description of the reduced models in terms of gauge invariant field combinations naturally leads to higher derivative models, contrary to lower spin cases ($s\le 2$). For both $s=3$ and $s=4$ we have a rather peculiar massless limit. Although their particle content corresponds to the $\pm j$ helicities with $j=0,1, \cdots s$, as expected, they appear intertwined in a non trivial way preventing diagonalization through any local field redefinition.

entry.title: SmoQyElPhQMC.jl: An open-source Julia package for efficient and scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled models
entry.summary: We introduce version 1.0 of the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package, an open-source Julia code for performing scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled model Hamiltonians. SmoQyElPhQMC.jl is built upon the SmoQyDQMC.jl codebase and implements improved versions of the algorithms presented in [B. Cohen-Stead \textit{et al}., Phys. Rev. E 105, 065302 (2022)] to enable (near-linear) scalable simulations of a broad class of uncorrelated $e$-ph models both in system size and inverse temperature. By extending the functionality of the flexible scripting interface introduced in SmoQyDQMC.jl, the SmoQyElPhQMC.jl package continues to allow users to adapt it to different workflows and interface with other software packages in the Julia ecosystem. The code for this package can be downloaded from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/SmoQySuite/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl or installed using the Julia package manager. The online documentation, including examples, can be obtained from our documentation page at https://smoqysuite.github.io/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl/stable/.

entry.title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
entry.summary: We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2. In the end, we discuss how the framework could be extended and compute the same predictions for the bicubic up to genus 9.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event: A Minimal $U(1)_B$ Dark Sector and Its Experimental Tests
entry.summary: The $248$ keV nuclear-recoil candidate reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) motivates an inelastic dark matter (DM) interpretation, in which scattering converts the DM particle into a slightly heavier state. We provide a comprehensive study of this interpretation in an anomaly-free model of gauged baryon number, where a new vector boson, $Z_B$, mediates interactions between DM and quarks. Breaking the baryonic gauge symmetry generates the new particle masses and a small splitting between two DM states, while a residual symmetry keeps the lighter state stable. We identify regions compatible with the LZ candidate, the observed DM abundance, and current ATLAS and CMS dijet constraints. Within the scanned domain, these regions span DM masses $m_χ\simeq0.19$-$4.5$ TeV, mediator masses $M_{Z_B}\simeq0.05$-$5.0$ TeV, and gauge couplings $g_B\simeq0.004$-$0.74$, with correlated values of these parameters. A representative thermal solution has $m_χ=1$ TeV, $M_{Z_B}=1.44$ TeV, $g_B\simeq0.228$, and a mass splitting of $300$ keV. A small electroweak mixing allows the heavier DM state to decay rapidly, suppressing unwanted signals from its surviving population. This interpretation can be tested through complementary measurements: additional LZ and XENONnT data can establish whether the high-energy recoil signal persists, ATLAS and CMS Run-3 dijet searches can probe the mediator mass and coupling, and a dedicated IceCube analysis of four-quark final states can test DM capture and annihilation in the Sun. Together, these measurements can test complementary parts of the surviving region and assess whether the LZ candidate is consistent with this interpretation.

entry.title: A Pipeline for the AI-Assisted Analysis of Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer Observations of Black Hole X-ray Binaries and Limits on Their Polarization Variability
entry.summary: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) has opened a new window into the high-energy Universe, with the capability to measure the arrival time, arrival direction, energy, and, for the first time with the required sensitivity, the polarization of X-rays from black holes, neutron stars, and other cosmic sources of X-rays. In this paper, we discuss the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents for the analysis of IXPE data. The pipeline combines an immutable code base with evolving knowledge databases. The generation of analysis projects makes use of a literature data base to judge the novelty of the proposed analysis projects. We emphasize that the analysis requires two types of expert knowledge: detailed instructions about how to reduce the X-ray data, and expert knowledge about how to interpret the results. We employ several levels of auditors that scrutinize the analysis plan, the analysis scripts, and the analysis results for data and method adequacy. The pipeline includes a staggered approach to interpret the analysis results. We present exemplary results from the pipeline applied to IXPE observations of Black Hole X-ray Binaries (BHXRBs) including comparisons of results from the analysis pipeline with published results and a systematic search for polarization degree and polarization angle variability in long IXPE observations. We critically discuss the performance of the pipeline and future avenues for improving it.

entry.title: Exact SU($N$) symmetry resolution of bosonic Hubbard models: general boson-fermion mappings and flat-band singlet-cluster states
entry.summary: We show how to perform exact diagonalization of SU($N$)-symmetric Bose-Hubbard models separately in each irreducible representation of SU($N$), by exploiting the Howe duality between U($L$) and U($N$). Three structural consequences follow for any lattice and any Hamiltonian built from the U($L$) generators: (i) the spectrum in a given orbital sector is independent of $N$ and of the particle statistics, (ii) the canonical partition functions for bosons and fermions obey the exact identity $Z_{\mathrm{b}}(-N)=(-1)^{N_\mathrm{b}}Z_{\mathrm{f}}(N)$, (iii) with unfrustrated hopping the groundstate is always a color ferromagnet, so that the color-resolved method we introduce is useful to study excited sectors, frustrated lattices and finite temperatures. As applications, we first derive the finite-temperature phase diagram of attractive SU($N$) bosons on few-site rings at large $N$ for arbitrary filling. We then show the emergence of singlet-cluster states from frustrated hopping, the counterpart of fermionic ferromagnetism, with the example of the sawtooth and kagome lattice.

entry.title: Collider and direct detection as key probes of asymmetric dark matter: Signals from a compressed Inert Higgs doublet
entry.summary: The cosmic imbalance of particles over antiparticles may be inherited by the dark matter in a certain class of asymmetric dark matter models. In this article, we thoroughly investigate the signatures of the minimal realization of this idea. In this model a new (stable) inert Higgs, $H'$, plays the role of the mediator that facilitates the asymmetry transfer from the visible to the dark sector. It also constitutes a small dark matter sub-component, while the dominant component stems from a singlet scalar asymmetry. A combination of phenomenological and cosmological constraints requires this new inert Higgs doublet to be quite light $46\,{\rm GeV}<m_{H'}< 580\,{\rm GeV}$ and its spectrum rather compressed, $ΔM = m_{H^\pm}-m_{H_0} \lesssim 1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $δm = m_{A_0}-m_{H_0}\lesssim 5\,{\rm MeV}$. Therefore its charged component can be relatively long-lived on collider length-scales. By recasting searches for compressed Higgsinos at the LHC, we derive new limits on this particle and show that, while at present most of the parameter space for this state is still unconstrained, large and key regions of parameter space will be tested at the HL-LHC by a combination of searches for disappearing charged tracks and displaced soft tracks. Quite remarkably, the lifetime of the charged component of the doublet can be correlated with the dark matter interaction rate at direct detection experiments and we show that the next generation of direct detection experiments has a unique sensitivity to the parameter space in the model. The fact that a small neutral mass splitting is a prediction of the asymmetric setup makes it an interesting candidate to account for the high energy nuclear recoil event recently reported by the LZ experiment. More generally, our detailed phenomenological study holds for any dark matter model involving an inert Higgs doublet with mass below 580 GeV.
